original_question: Fix a prime p > 2 and a power q of p. Let L(u, f, psi) be the Artin-Schreier L-function attached to a rational function f in F_q(x) and an additive character psi. For the families AS_d^ord = {f = h/g : h, g in F_q[x], (g,h)=1, g squarefree, deg f = max(deg h, deg g) = d, deg g in {d, d-1}}, AS_d^0 = {f in F_q[x] : deg f = d, (d,p)=1}, and AS_d^{0,odd} = {f in F_q[x] : deg f = d, f(x) = -f(-x), (d,2p)=1}, with q fixed and d -> infinity and with M_k denoting the k-th moment of L(q^(1/2), f, psi), compute the listed low moments and extend the 1-level density of zeros beyond the currently stated support ranges: for AS_d^ord, compute M1 through M6 and prove 1-level density for support of phi-hat inside (-1-delta, 1+delta) or (-2-delta, 2+delta); for AS_d^0, compute M1 through M4 and prove 1-level density for support inside (-(2-2/p)-delta, 2-2/p+delta); for AS_d^{0,odd}, compute M1 and M2 and prove 1-level density for support inside (-(1-1/p)-delta, 1-1/p+delta).
target_in_paper: Problem (20) in the Problems section: "Compute moments for families of Artin-Schreier L-functions and improve results on 1-level zero density."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the exact three Artin-Schreier families appearing in Problem (20), keeps the fixed-q, d→∞ regime, includes the same low-moment goals for each family, and reproduces the same enlarged support ranges for the desired 1-level density results.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:2405.17800 is Problem (20) on page 10; the paper does not state this as a theorem, proposition, or conjecture.
A fully stand-alone version should say explicitly that the 1-level density is taken with respect to a Schwartz test function φ.
It should explicitly state that one is asking for the limiting 1-level density as d→∞ with q fixed.
For AS_d^ord, the quantifier in the paper is "for some δ>0" in each of the two alternative support extensions; this should be preserved exactly.
The moment notation should be made explicit as a family average, not only by naming M_k informally.
To be fully self-contained, the question should define the central-value evaluation of the Artin-Schreier L-function rather than only writing a bare symbol L(...,f,ψ).

The paper’s intent is narrowly the listed low moments and the listed support improvements for these three families only; a refined question should not broaden to higher-level densities, more moments, or other Artin-Schreier strata.
refined_question:
Fix a prime p>2 and a power q of p. Let L(u,f,ψ) be the Artin-Schreier L-function attached to a rational function f∈F_q(x) and an additive character ψ. For the three families
AS_d^0={f∈F_q[x]: deg f=d, (d,p)=1},
AS_d^{0,odd}={f∈F_q[x]: deg f=d, f(x)=-f(-x), (d,2p)=1},
and
AS_d^{ord}={f=h/g: h,g∈F_q[x], (g,h)=1, g squarefree, deg f=max(deg h,deg g)=d, deg g∈{d,d-1}},
let M_k(F_d):=(1/|F_d|)∑_{f∈F_d} L_c(f,ψ)^k denote the k-th family moment at the central value L_c(f,ψ). In the regime where q is fixed and d→∞, determine the limiting 1-level density of zeros with respect to a Schwartz test function φ for the support ranges requested in Problem (20)—namely: for AS_d^{ord}, either supp φ̂⊂(-1-δ,1+δ) for some δ>0 or supp φ̂⊂(-2-δ,2+δ) for some δ>0; for AS_d^0, supp φ̂⊂(-(2-2/p)-δ, 2-2/p+δ); and for AS_d^{0,odd}, supp φ̂⊂(-(1-1/p)-δ, 1-1/p+δ)—and compute the corresponding low moments M_1,...,M_6 for AS_d^{ord}, M_1,...,M_4 for AS_d^0, and M_1,M_2 for AS_d^{0,odd}.
justification: The draft is targeting Problem (20) almost verbatim, but it needs to be tightened into a single self-contained question. The paper itself is a problem list, so the correct anchor is Problem (20), not a neighboring theorem. I therefore kept the scope exactly at the three named families, the fixed-q large-d limit, the listed low moments, and the three specified support-extension targets. I also made explicit the family-average nature of M_k and the role of the Schwartz test function in the 1-level density, while avoiding any broader reformulation in terms of general random-matrix conjectures or higher-level densities, which would go beyond the paper’s stated problem.
